To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
graphene is a $\pi$ electron macromolecule and that the $\pi$-electron spectrum of graphene and its derivatives is described by the exact solutions to the eigenvalue equation.

the exact solution to a simple $\pi$-electron problem provides a complete description of the electronic structure of the graphene sheet and graphene ribbons and tubes of any width and chirality, and that the graphene tori are described by the same problem in the case of a small torus radius.

the electronic spectrum of graphene sheets, ribbons, tubes, and tori is a set of $N$ bands of the width of $2\pi$ and the energy gap of $4\pi$ between them, where $N$ is the number of carbon atoms in the respective structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of the exact theory of $\pi$-electron spectra for graphene and its derivatives, which allows one to calculate and analyze their electronic structure, and to predict their optical and other properties.
the exact description and classification of $\pi$-electron spectra of graphene sheets, graphene ribbons, carbon nanotubes and graphene tori.
the exact solutions of eigenvalue problems for graphene structures of various shapes and sizes, and with the comparison of the obtained results with those of the widely used models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the exact solution to a simple $\pi$-electron model of graphene allows to describe the electronic structure of the most important graphene nanostructures and to understand the origin of their characteristic electronic properties, including the edge states and the band gaps.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the $\pi$-electron spectrum of graphene sheets, ribbons and tubes is described by a simple and exact model, which is based on the $\pi$-$\pi$ interaction between graphene layers.
the model of graphene macromolecule is the simplest model that is capable to describe the electronic structure of all graphene structures of finite size.

the exact solutions for the $\pi$-electron spectra of the above structures, which can be obtained within the framework of the revisited model, are in a good agreement with experimental data and the results of numerical simulations, and the exact expressions of detectable observables are in a better agreement with experimental data than the corresponding results of other models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the $\pi$-electron spectrum of graphene macromolecule can be calculated exactly for the structures of any complexity.
the exact model allows to describe the electronic structure of any graphene-based nanostructure in the same way, without the need for the introduction of additional fitting parameters.

the exact solution for graphene sheets, ribbons and tubes can be obtained by solving a simple eigenvalue problem for a matrix of the size $2\times 2N\times 2\times 1$ and the solution for graphene tori can be obtained by diagonalizing the matrix of the size $\cal N\times \cal N$.
